messages:
maya: Heads up — ran the HF->Redwood tokenizer conversion for the new 7B spm model and seeing weird short-sequence regressions in the smoke evals. not just quality, some tokens seem shifted.

sven: Can you paste the failure example? quick repro?

maya: minimal repro: prompt 'User: Hi\nAssistant:' then generation starts with '\\u0123' weird char and then a repetition of 'User:' after 8 tokens. Fails on quantized int8 and fp16.

jordan: that sounds like special-token aliasing — HF sometimes maps chat-special tokens to high ids that collide with BPE offsets during conversion. did you check special_tokens_map?

maya: yep. converter output shows: 
```
"<unk>": 0
"<s>": 1
"</s>": 2
"<pad>": 3
"<|user|>": 50256
"<|assistant|>": 50257
```
but the model vocab length is 50260 and our BPE-add offset is +3 in the conversion path, so the mapped ids are off by 3 in the final tokenizer.json.

li: also check unicode normalization — spm->bpe converters differ (SentencePiece normalizes to NFKC by default, but our tokenizer expects NFC). uncontrolled normalization can change merge boundaries and cause merge collisions. saw this with non-ascii punctuation.

arjun: any config.json mismatches? special tokens in config vs tokenizer.json mismatch will cause the runtime to use the wrong indices during chat template assembly.

maya: config.json had "bos_token" : "<s>" and chat template used role tokens as literal strings, but the tokenizer's "added_tokens" list had aliases: ["<|user|>", "<|assistant|>"] — during conversion they got appended instead of mapped, so offsets moved.

jordan: two-prong fix I recommend: 1) run conversion with explicit special token mapping JSON and preserve indices (don't append), 2) force consistent unicode normalization to NFC before applying merges.

sven: can you run quick script to remap and retokenize smoke prompt? i can run an eval job if you push the tokenizer artifact.

maya: pushing a build to gs://redwood-dev-tokenizers/7b-spm-conv/1780056789/ now. converter flags I used: `python convert_spm.py --spm model.spm --out tokenizer.json --append-specials` 

maya: changed command to: `python convert_spm.py --spm model.spm --out tokenizer.json --map-specials special_map.json --normalize NFC --preserve-indices` and repushed. special_map.json contains explicit id mappings for the role tokens.

ci-bot: ci: evals/short-seq-regression triggered for build 1780056789 — queued on gpu-pool-3. ETA ~12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

arjun: thanks. one more note — quantization kernels assume contiguous id ranges for added tokens in our runtime. if we keep specials scattered at high ids it causes suboptimal cache placement and can give strange prefix cache reuse. prefer consolidating role tokens into contiguous low ids if possible.

maya: agreed. after remap + NFC normalization the smoke eval passed locally (pass rate 99.4 -> 99.8 on short-seq tests). pushing to CI to validate across quantized configs.

sven: good catch. can we add a small unit test in model-onboarding that verifies special token indices preserved after conversion and that roundtrip encode/decode of chat templates returns identical token ids?

jordan: yes — add test under eng-ml/models/tests/tokenizer_roundtrip_test.py with cases: normal ascii, emoji, combining marks, and chat template role joiners.

maya: i'll open a PR with the converter flag defaults and test. leaving notes in PR about NFC vs NFKC and why we chose NFC for runtime consistency.

li: tiny FYI — document the rationale in model-onboarding checklist: "when converting SPM->BPE ensure normalization=NFC, supply explicit special token id map, and validate contiguous block allocation for role tokens if using quantized runtime".

maya: filing that now. thanks all :tada:
